_comment: Character -> tile id, per world. A level picks its world with a top-level "tileset" key; omitting it means "jungle". See docs/adr/002-level-format.md.
_comment_shared: Characters that mean the same tile in every world: water, the movement verbs (currents, drafts, breakable walls), switch blocks and the hub. A tileset may not redefine one -- tests/test_level_format.gd enforces that.
_comment_roles: Every tileset binds the same twelve role characters to its own art, so '#' is always this world's ground and '|' is always its ladder: '#' ground cap, the world's primary solid; 'S' the alt solid it autotiles against; 'd' the fill under the cap; 's' a second, harder solid; '=' one-way platform; '|' ladder / climbable; '^' hazard; 'c' breakable block; 'L' background wall; 'T' background column; 'r' background accent; 'X' background deep / void.
_comment_verbs: The drafts read lowercase-is-water, uppercase-is-air: '>' '<' 'u' 'v' are currents and '}' '{' the fast pair; ')' '(' 'U' 'V' are gusts and drafts and '*' the strong updraft. Breakables by what they are: 'k' cracked stone, 'j' cracked dirt, 'm' termite wall, 'O' luminous wall, 'o' rubble.
_comment_legend: 'legend' below is the resolved jungle tileset -- shared plus tilesets.jungle, nothing else. It is kept because tools/reachability.py and tools/build_hub.py read this file's 'legend' key directly and both only ever look at jungle levels and the hub. It is not a second source of truth: tests/test_level_format.gd fails if it drifts from shared + jungle.
